title: Immediate Regime-Pair Closure History Diagnostic V1

scope.purpose: Test whether causal state history before an observed A-to-B regime transition improves prediction that the next completed regime returns to A, forming the corrected primitive A-to-B-to-A closure.
scope.interpretation: Fixed-model structural sensitivity diagnostic only. It cannot validate numeric regime identities, semantic loop dictionaries, price direction, payoff, or trading edge.

source_identity.bar_timestamp_convention: provider timestamp is bar start; completed-bar availability is timestamp plus five minutes
source_identity.volume_meaning: provider-reported historical_volume activity field; not order flow, quote flow, exchange-wide volume, or executable liquidity

state_model_binding.semantic_limitation: Numeric labels are evaluated only inside the frozen fitted representation. Pair identity must not be projected across refits.

population.decision_unit: first completed bar assigned to each new causal state run
population.required_history: at least one fully completed preceding state run in the same contiguous symbol-session segment
population.target: next completed state equals the immediately preceding state
population.primitive_loop_semantics: A-to-B-to-A with A not equal to B; orientation retained and the unordered pair reported separately

hypothesis.primary: M5_LAST_FIVE_STATES improves 2025 paired log loss and Brier score over M2_IMMEDIATE_PAIR for immediate pair-closure prediction.
hypothesis.descriptive: Some A-to-B orientations have closure rates different from other predecessors of the same current state, with directionally consistent 2024 and 2025 estimates.
hypothesis.rescue_policy: No posterior, duration, previous-loop, stock, or clock diagnostic may rescue failure of the M5-versus-M2 primary comparison.

chronology.development_folds: expanding calendar-month folds; first three complete 2024 months train-only

requirements: M5 assessment log loss is lower than M2
M5 assessment Brier score is lower than M2
paired session-block 95% lower bound for log-loss improvement is above zero
improvement is positive in at least three of four 2025 calendar quarters
at least 90 percent of leave-one-stock-out log-loss improvements are positive
hard-state sensitivity has the same point-estimate direction
